newsitem.title: USA: Omnipoint sees advantage in simple pricing.
newsitem.headline: Omnipoint sees advantage in simple pricing.

text.p: Wireless phone company Omnipoint Corp, which launched its Personal Communications Services (PCS) package in New York on Thursday, said it sees a great advantage from a simple pricing plan.
"There will be no asterisks or fine print in our advertising, not now, not ever," Omnipoint President George Schmitt said.

Unlike most cellular carriers, Omnipoint will not add long distance or other charges on to air time charges, he said. He said Omnipoint would not use contracts to retain customers, and those unhappy within 30 days would get a refund.
"We expect some people who are frustrated with dropped call and system busy messages to switch over," he said.
Schmitt also expected the security offered by the service's encrypted signals to attract lawyers and bankers who steered away from cellular service because of the fear of electronic eavesdropping.
Call rates start at $0.25 per minute for local calls made off peak and on weekends. Calls for anywhere in the United States and Canada are $0.69 per minute.
Five dollars of usage is included with each service package, with an automatic five percent discount for every $50 worth of billed usage, to a 25 percent maximum.
International calls range from $0.99 per minute to $1.99 per minute. Omnipoint uses the Global System for Mobile communications (GSM) standard which is common outside the U.S.
He said users would soon be able to take their phones to almost all of Europe and eventually 100 countries and call home. The bill would arrive, in dollars, when they return.

Battery life for the new phones allows between one and 2-1/2 hours of conversation and 30-72 hours on standby mode -- when calls can be received. This is about twice as long as existing cellular phones.
The phones, which start at $199, are supplied by Telefon AB L.M. Ericsson of Sweden, Nokia Group of Finland, and Motorola Inc of the U.S., and weigh between seven and eight ounces (210-240 grams).

Handsets from other manufacturers will follow soon, Schmitt said. He said a new generation of phones weighing less than seven ounces would be available in a year or so, including a GSM version of Motorola's Startac phone.

Omnipoint's license areas cover 40 million people in the north east, though the service launched on Thursday covers only metropolitan New York. However, roaming agreements are in place with other U.S. users of GSM systems.

This will soon allow Omnipoint customers to use their phones in parts of Alabama through BellSouth Corp, parts of California through Pacific Telesis Group and the Washington-Baltimore region of American Personal Communications. -- Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1610
